source: Dr Benitex CHM121 Revision Series 2 — cleaned and independently verified MCQs; ambiguous, incomplete, five-option, and structurally invalid source questions excluded

questions.question: Which of the following is not a class of organic compounds?
questions.explanation: Amides, nitro compounds, and carbonyl compounds are recognized classes of organic compounds. “Electro compounds” is not a standard class.

questions.question: Which of the following does not come under the organic addition reaction?
questions.explanation: Halogenation, hydrohalogenation, and hydration are addition reactions of unsaturated compounds. Dehydration is an elimination reaction.

questions.question: Which of the following compound is yielded from the reduction of nitroalkanes?
questions.explanation: Reduction of a nitroalkane converts the nitro group to an amino group, giving an amine.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to prepare Benzoyl chloride from benzoic acid?
questions.explanation: Thionyl chloride converts carboxylic acids into the corresponding acid chlorides; benzoic acid therefore gives benzoyl chloride.

questions.question: Isomerism that arises out of the difference in spatial arrangement of atoms or groups about the doubly bonded carbon atoms are called? (In specific)
questions.explanation: Restricted rotation about a carbon-carbon double bond can give cis/trans or E/Z geometrical isomerism.

questions.question: Which among the following does not exhibit geometric isomerism?
questions.explanation: A terminal alkene such as 1-hexene has two identical hydrogen substituents on one double-bond carbon, so E/Z isomerism is impossible.

questions.question: Which among the following is formed when an alcohol is dehydrated?
questions.explanation: Acid-catalysed dehydration of an alcohol removes water and commonly forms an alkene.

questions.question: Identify the chiral molecule among the following.
questions.explanation: 2-Pentanol has a stereogenic carbon attached to OH, H, methyl, and propyl groups.

questions.question: A fat on hydrolysis would yield?
questions.explanation: Alkaline hydrolysis (saponification) of fats produces glycerol and salts of fatty acids, which are soaps.

questions.question: The element least likely to be found in an organic compound is ...
questions.explanation: Nitrogen, sulfur, and oxygen are common elements in organic compounds. Silicon occurs in organosilicon compounds but is much less commonly encountered in ordinary organic compounds.

questions.question: Identify the correct statement which is related to aromatic hydrocarbon?
options: It has a sigma and two pi bonds
It has a sigma and delocalized pi bonds
questions.answer: It has a sigma and delocalized pi bonds
questions.explanation: Aromatic systems contain sigma bonds plus a delocalized π-electron system spread over the conjugated ring.

questions.question: Aliphatic compound is the other name for _________
questions.explanation: In the terminology used in the source, aliphatic compounds are open-chain (acyclic) compounds.

questions.question: Which among the following is not an example of Acyclic compound?
questions.explanation: Cyclopropane is a cyclic compound because its carbon atoms form a ring; the other choices are acyclic.

questions.question: In crystallization, the compound dissolved in a solvent is more soluble in what temperature?
questions.explanation: Recrystallization commonly relies on a substance being much more soluble in the hot solvent than in the cold solvent.

questions.question: The substituent groups that are commonly associated with benzene ring are _________
questions.explanation: Phenyl (C6H5–) and benzyl (C6H5CH2–) are common substituent groups associated with aromatic chemistry.

questions.question: Which among these is not a structural isomer of the compound C4H8?
questions.explanation: But-3-ene is simply another numbering of but-1-ene, not a distinct structural isomer.

questions.question: Select the incorrect statement regarding alkenes.
options: In alkenes, the carbons are connected by pi bonds
Alkenes have almost same physical properties as that of the alkanes
Alkenes are less reactive than alkanes
questions.answer: Alkenes are less reactive than alkanes
questions.explanation: The carbon-carbon double bond makes alkenes generally more chemically reactive than alkanes, and alkenes can undergo polymerization.

questions.question: Acetylene has a total of
questions.explanation: Acetylene (HC≡CH) contains two C–H sigma bonds and one C–C sigma bond, plus two π bonds.

questions.question: Compounds in which carbon use only sp3 hybrid orbitals for bond formation is …….
questions.explanation: In propane, every carbon forms only single bonds and is therefore sp3-hybridized.

questions.question: When the carbon atom is sp2 hybridized, it is bonded to …
questions.explanation: An sp2-hybridized carbon has three sigma-bonding directions arranged approximately trigonal-planar, with one unhybridized p orbital.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a planar molecule
questions.explanation: The carbonyl group is planar, but acetone as a whole contains tetrahedral methyl groups whose hydrogens need not lie in the carbonyl plane.

questions.question: Which molecule has a non-zero dipole moment
questions.explanation: CHCl3 is unsymmetrical, so its bond dipoles do not cancel completely. Cl2, CO2, and CCl4 have zero net dipole moments.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds will have the lowest dipole moment
questions.explanation: CCl4 is tetrahedrally symmetrical, so the four C–Cl bond dipoles cancel and the net dipole moment is zero.

questions.question: The following statements are not true about Lassaigne test except
options: used to test for the presence of oxygen and carbon
used to test for functional group
questions.explanation: Lassaigne's sodium-fusion procedure converts covalently bound heteroatoms into ionic species and is fundamentally a reductive fusion process.

questions.question: A constant melting point mixture can be referred to as ….. while a constant boiling point mixture can be referred to as…..
questions.explanation: A eutectic mixture has a constant melting point, while an azeotrope has constant-boiling composition.

questions.question: …........analysis can be used to determine those elements present in a compound.
questions.explanation: Qualitative analysis identifies which elements or ions are present; quantitative analysis determines amounts.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is an alicyclic compound
questions.explanation: Cyclobutene is a non-aromatic cyclic compound and is therefore alicyclic.

questions.question: A certain neutral compound Y reacts with sodium metal to evolve a colourless gax Z. Further tests show that compound Y decolorizes acidified potassium heptaoxodichromate (Vi) from orange to green. What is the identity of Y and Z respectively?
questions.explanation: Alcohols react with sodium metal to release hydrogen gas, and an oxidizable alcohol can reduce acidified dichromate from orange to green.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds will show negative towards iodoform test
questions.explanation: Ethanol, ethanal, and propanone give the iodoform reaction. Propan-1-ol does not contain the required CH3CO– or CH3CH(OH)– arrangement.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds will form a grey precipitate of Ag in a test tube?
questions.explanation: An aldehyde such as acetaldehyde reduces Tollens' reagent, depositing metallic silver as a silver mirror or precipitate.

questions.question: A certain compound W reacts with alkanols to produce X which has a fruity smell. Further tests show that W reacts with sodium hydrogen carbonate to evolve a colourless gas Y. What are the identities of W, X and Y?
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids react with alcohols to form fruity-smelling esters, and with sodium hydrogen carbonate to release carbon dioxide.

questions.question: An unknown sample Z decolorizes bromine water and further tests show it restores the magenta(pink) colour of Schiff's reagent. Z could be......
questions.explanation: The C=C bond decolorizes bromine water, while the aldehyde group in but-2-enal gives a positive Schiff test.

questions.question: A 0.152g of an organic compound X containing only C, H and O produces 0.223g of CO2 and 0.091g of H2O on combustion. what is the empirical formula of compound X
questions.explanation: The combustion data give approximately equal moles of C and O and twice as many moles of H, giving the empirical formula CH2O.

questions.question: The effect of attracting or repelling of electrons in sigma bonds is referred to as......
questions.explanation: The inductive effect is the permanent polarization transmitted through sigma bonds because of electron-attracting or electron-releasing substituents.

questions.question: Heterolytic bond fission is favoured by the following except.......
options: presence of resonance and inductive effect
questions.explanation: Heterolysis is favoured by polar environments and charge-stabilizing effects. Free-radical initiators instead promote homolytic cleavage.

questions.question: Homolytic fission of C-C bond leads to the formation of ….
questions.explanation: Homolytic cleavage splits the bonding electron pair equally, leaving one electron on each carbon and producing radicals.

questions.question: The order of stability of carbonium ion and free radicals is
questions.explanation: For simple alkyl carbocations and radicals, increasing alkyl substitution generally increases stability through hyperconjugation and inductive donation.

questions.question: Which statement is correct……………
options: energy is released when a bond breaks
a sigma bond results from attraction of protons and electrons
energy is released when a bond forms
questions.answer: energy is released when a bond forms
questions.explanation: Bond formation releases energy because the bonded state is lower in energy than the separated atoms. Bond breaking requires energy.

questions.question: Which describes the bond strength or dissociation energy
options: energy required to break a bond
energy released when a bond breaks
energy released when a bond is formed
questions.answer: energy required to break a bond
questions.explanation: Bond dissociation energy is the energy required to break a specified bond, usually homolytically in the gas phase.

questions.question: An electrophile acts as a ……. When it reacts with nucleophile while a nucleophile acts as a …… whe it reacts with an electrophile….
questions.explanation: An electrophile accepts an electron pair and is therefore a Lewis acid; a nucleophile donates an electron pair and is a Lewis base.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect
options: electrons move toward positively charged locations
an electron rich atom is called an electrophile
a nucleophile has a pair of electrons it can share
questions.answer: an electron rich atom is called an electrophile
questions.explanation: Electrophiles are electron-deficient species. Electron-rich species that donate electron pairs are nucleophiles.

questions.question: Identify the one which shows E-Z mechanism?
questions.explanation: 3-Methylpent-2-ene has two different substituents on each alkene carbon, allowing E/Z stereoisomerism.

questions.question: 4-chlorobut-1-ene is the name of which among the following alkenes?
questions.explanation: Numbering from the double-bond end gives but-1-ene with chlorine at carbon 4: CH2=CH-CH2-CH2Cl, equivalent to the listed structure.

questions.question: Ethylene on reaction with bromine forms which among the following product?
questions.explanation: Bromine adds across the C=C bond of ethene to form 1,2-dibromoethane.

questions.question: Which among the following is not an alkane isomer with 6 carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: Neopentane has five carbon atoms (C5H12), whereas the other choices are C6 alkane structures.

questions.question: Which homologous series can be produced from the protonation of grignard reagents ....
questions.explanation: A Grignard reagent R–MgX is protonated at carbon to give RH, an alkane.

questions.question: Grignard reagents can be produced from which of the following
options: Magnesium powder with alkyl halides in dry ether
Sodium metal with alkyl halides in dry ether
Mercury with alkyl halides in dry ether
questions.answer: Magnesium powder with alkyl halides in dry ether
questions.explanation: Grignard reagents are formed by reacting an alkyl or aryl halide with magnesium in dry ether.

questions.question: The breaking down of a heavy alkane molecules in the presence of heat, pressure and a catalyst to give smaller alkanes and alkenes is referred to as.....
questions.explanation: Pyrolysis or cracking breaks larger hydrocarbon molecules into smaller molecules, including alkanes and alkenes.

questions.question: The Halogenation of alkanes proceed via what mechanism
questions.explanation: Alkane halogenation under light or heat proceeds through a free-radical chain substitution mechanism.

questions.question: The IUPAC name of the compound CH3CH2CH2N(CH3)2
questions.explanation: The nitrogen is bonded to a propyl group and two methyl groups, giving the source's name N,N-dimethylpropylamine.

questions.question: Which one of the following compound is obtained by the oxidation of secondary alcohol by [O]
questions.explanation: Oxidation of a secondary alcohol produces a ketone.

questions.question: The reaction of carboxylic acids with alcohols catalyzed by conc H2SO4 is called ……
questions.explanation: Acid-catalysed reaction of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol forms an ester and water and is called esterification.

questions.question: The oxidation state of oxygen in potassium superoxide(KO2) is
questions.explanation: In KO2, potassium is +1, so the O2 group is −1 overall. Each oxygen therefore has an average oxidation state of −1/2.

questions.question: When heptane undergoes complete combustion how many moles of carbon(iv)oxide (CO2) is produced?
questions.explanation: Complete combustion of C7H16 produces seven CO2 molecules per mole of heptane because each carbon atom becomes one CO2 molecule.
questions.working:
C7H16 + 11O2 → 7CO2 + 8H2O.
Therefore, 1 mol of heptane produces 7 mol of CO2.
Answer = 7 mol, matching the second option.

questions.question: For reactions involving electrophilic addition the predominant product can be predicted by ……
questions.explanation: For addition of an unsymmetrical reagent such as HX to an unsymmetrical alkene, Markovnikov's rule predicts the major product under the usual conditions.

questions.question: Fullerenes are composed of 60 carbon atoms joined together by single and double bonds to form a hollow sphere with …..
questions.explanation: Buckminsterfullerene, C60, has a truncated-icosahedron structure containing 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons.

questions.question: The third fraction obtained during fractional distillation of crude oil is……
questions.explanation: Using the simplified fraction sequence represented by the source, petrol is followed by kerosene and then diesel oil.

questions.question: Which of the following alkanes has the highest melting point.
questions.explanation: Among these C5 alkane isomers, the highly symmetrical neopentane (2,2-dimethylpropane) packs particularly well in the solid state and has the highest melting point.

questions.question: What type of isomerism exists between CH3CHCl2 and CH2ClCH2Cl
questions.explanation: Both compounds have the same carbon skeleton and functional groups, but the chlorine atoms occupy different positions.

questions.question: Coal distillation in the absence of air to give coke, coal gas and liquid by-products is called ….
questions.explanation: Heating coal in the absence of air decomposes it into coke, coal gas, tar and other products; this is destructive distillation.

questions.question: Hydrocarbons are generally ……. in non-polar solvents but ….. in polar solvents
questions.explanation: Non-polar hydrocarbons dissolve preferentially in non-polar solvents and are generally poorly soluble in polar solvents.

questions.question: Methane reacts with chlorine in the presence of sunlight to give ……
questions.explanation: Successive free-radical chlorination of methane can produce chloromethane, dichloromethane, chloroform, and carbon tetrachloride.

questions.question: Dienes is the name given to compounds with ….
questions.explanation: A diene is a hydrocarbon containing two carbon-carbon double bonds.

questions.question: Which reagent converts an aldehyde specifically into a primary alcohol?
questions.explanation: Sodium borohydride reduces an aldehyde carbonyl group to a primary alcohol without being an oxidizing reagent.

questions.question: Which test distinguishes aldehydes from ketones in most cases?
questions.explanation: Aldehydes generally reduce Tollens' reagent to metallic silver, whereas ordinary ketones do not.

questions.question: The ozonolysis of alkenes yields..
questions.explanation: Reductive ozonolysis cleaves the C=C bond to form aldehydes and/or ketones depending on the alkene substitution.

questions.question: The reaction of Br2 with alkenes in organic solvent in the dark follows what mechanism
questions.explanation: Bromine adds electrophilically across an alkene double bond through a bromonium-ion-type intermediate.

questions.question: The primary function of Zn/CH3COOH in the ozonolysis of alkenes is...
options: To enhance the oxidation of ketones
To prevent oxidation of ketones to carboxylic acids
To prevent oxidation of aldehydes to carboxylic acids
questions.answer: To prevent oxidation of aldehydes to carboxylic acids
questions.explanation: Reductive work-up with Zn/acetic acid prevents aldehydes formed during ozonolysis from being further oxidized to carboxylic acids.

questions.question: The ozonolysis of a compound X gives ethanal and propanal. What is X?
questions.explanation: Cleavage of pent-2-ene, CH3CH=CHCH2CH3, gives ethanal from one alkene carbon and propanal from the other.

questions.question: An organic process involving smaller units combining to form larger molecules of high molecular weights is best described as .....
questions.explanation: Polymerization joins monomer units to form larger molecules with high molecular mass.

questions.question: The electrophillic addition of HA molecule to unsymmetrical alkenes and alkynes follows....
questions.explanation: Markovnikov's rule predicts the usual orientation of electrophilic addition of HX or related HA reagents to unsymmetrical unsaturated compounds.

questions.question: Alkynes can be prepared by the following processes except...
options: Reaction of calcium carbide with water
questions.explanation: Vicinal and geminal dihalides can undergo double dehydrohalogenation to form alkynes, and calcium carbide reacts with water to form acetylene. “Markownikoff elimination” is not a standard alkyne-preparation method.

questions.question: Which of the following alkynes is terminal...
questions.explanation: Propyne, CH3C≡CH, has a hydrogen directly attached to a triple-bond carbon and is therefore a terminal alkyne.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is not aromatic?
questions.explanation: Cyclobutadiene has 4 π electrons and is antiaromatic when planar, so it is not aromatic.

questions.question: What is the major product when benzene is nitrated using a mixture of concentrated HNO₃ and H₂SO₄?
questions.explanation: The nitrating mixture generates the nitronium ion, NO2+, which substitutes for hydrogen on benzene to form nitrobenzene.

questions.question: Which alkaline earth metal hydroxide is the least soluble in water?
questions.explanation: The solubility of alkaline-earth hydroxides generally increases down the group; magnesium hydroxide is the least soluble among these.

questions.question: Which of the following reacts most vigorously with water?
questions.explanation: Reactivity of alkali metals with water increases down the group because ionization becomes easier; cesium is the most vigorous of these choices.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a property of alkali metals?
options: They form basic oxides and hydroxides.
questions.explanation: Alkali metals are electropositive and have low ionization energies and form basic oxides/hydroxides. Strong hydrogen bonding is not a characteristic property of the metals.

questions.question: Which of the following alkaline earth metal salts is insoluble in water?
questions.explanation: Barium sulfate is highly insoluble in water, unlike the listed chlorides and nitrates and the soluble magnesium sulfate.

questions.question: When alkali metals react with cold water, which of the following statements is CORRECT?
options: They form metal oxides and hydrogen gas.
They form metal hydroxides and hydrogen gas.
They form metal hydrides and hydrogen gas.
They form metal halides and hydrogen gas
questions.answer: They form metal hydroxides and hydrogen gas.
questions.explanation: Alkali metals react with cold water to form the corresponding hydroxide and hydrogen gas.

questions.question: Which of the following oxidation states is most stable for copper in aqueous solution?
questions.explanation: Cu2+ is generally the more stable oxidation state of copper in ordinary aqueous solution, although Cu+ can be stabilized in suitable complexes or solids.

questions.question: Silver halides are insoluble in water, but dissolve in aqueous ammonia due to:
options: Reduction of Ag⁺ to metallic silver
questions.explanation: Ammonia coordinates to Ag+ to form the soluble diamminesilver(I) complex, shifting dissolution of suitable silver halides.

questions.question: Which allotrope of phosphorus is most stable at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Black phosphorus is the thermodynamically most stable allotrope of phosphorus at ordinary conditions, although red phosphorus is also much more stable than white phosphorus.
